subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which provider-safe error classes and maximum total latency should the shared OAuth refresh path retry before its existing failover behavior runs?
rationale: The requested behavior changes cross-provider authentication failure semantics and lock-held latency; current code distinguishes terminal reuse/auth failures from recoverable paths, but no established generic retry contract is evidenced.

options.title: Approve narrow transient retries
options.body: Retry only transport/timeouts and explicitly classified retryable server responses within a short shared budget, then preserve the existing final error and failover path.

options.title: Keep single-attempt refresh
options.body: Retain current locking and specialized recovery only, leaving ordinary transient failures to the existing failover and re-authentication behavior.

options.title: Define provider-owned policies
options.body: Require each OAuth provider adapter to expose its own retryable-error classification before introducing shared retries.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow transient retries
recommendation.body: Retry only transport/timeouts and explicitly classified retryable server responses within a short shared budget, then preserve the existing final error and failover path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their OAuth lifecycle refactor history is the strongest direct ownership signal for the shared refresh-policy boundary.
